name: artifact_explore
description: Act on the open 3D model (heart, eye, brain, animal cell, plant cell, DNA). action: separate (also 'expand', 'explode', 'take it apart': the parts glide apart, each named), assemble (put it back together), cut_open (cut it open to see inside), whole (undo the cut), xray (see through the outer layers), xray_off, focus (show one part solid and everything else see-through; give part, e.g. 'mitral valve', 'lens', 'frontal lobe'), unfocus, turn (degrees, default 30), reset (everything back as it was). Pass template too (heart, eye, brain, cell, plant_cell, dna) when the user names a model that isn't open: it opens it first and waits for it to load. The result lists the model's parts and its state; say in a few words what changed.

part.description: For focus: the part's name as the user said it.

degrees.description: For turn: how far, in degrees (positive turns it to the right). Default 30.

template.description: The model the user named, if it might not be the open one: heart, eye, brain, cell, plant_cell or dna.

name: artifact_press
description: Press one of the open artifact's own buttons, to play its walkthrough or animation: 'trace the blood', 'show the blood flow' / 'hide it', 'pause the beat' (heart); 'follow the light' (eye); 'tour the lobes' (brain); 'follow a protein' (cell); 'follow the sunlight' (plant cell); 'explain it', 'spin it' / 'stop spinning' (DNA); 'hide labels' / 'show labels'. Say it as the user did; the result says which button it pressed and, for a walkthrough, its captions in order with how long each is on screen: explain the steps in that order, one short sentence each, as they play. If nothing matches, the result lists the buttons there are.

button.description: The button as the user said it, or its label or id.

template.description: The model the user named, if it might not be the open one: heart, eye, brain, cell, plant_cell or dna.

name: artifact_describe
description: What's open right now and what it can do: the artifact's title, its named parts, its buttons, its walkthrough captions and notes, and its state (apart, cut open, X-ray, which part is in focus). Call it before explaining the open model or answering a question about it, so you talk about what's actually there.
